data.name: Benno
data.gender_notes: Benno is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name Binyamin meaning 'son of the right hand' or 'son of the south'. In German, Benno means 'solver of riddles'. In Christianity, it is the name of several saints. The name Benno carries the meaning “Son of the South” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Benno usually hope their child will grow to embody son of the south and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of wisdom and problem-solving abilities.
data.etymology: Benno belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of the South.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Benno total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Benno has a rich Germanic background, with its meaning alluding to the understanding of riddles signifying wisdom and intelligence. This cultural meaning can inspire individuals to strive towards intellectual growth and problem-solving abilities.
data.spiritual_significance: Benno, as a Christian name, carries the legacy of several revered saints, including St. Benno of Meissen, St. Benno of Palermo, and St. Benno of Osnabrück. These men dedicated their lives to the service of God and the betterment of their communities. The spiritual significance of the name Benno, therefore, signifies a life devoted to faith, service, and the pursuit of holiness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Benno: Derived from the Hebrew name "Ben-Oni," meaning "son of my sorrow." In Christianity, it symbolizes the bearing of one's cross and enduring suffering for the greater good.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Benno of Meissen (d. 1088) was a German Benedictine monk and bishop. The name Benno carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Benno remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Grace Benno in New York, United States credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Benno, which means "Son of the South". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
